_about: The home page's house: the items in it, what their marks say, and sales of similar items (each with its source). low/high are filled from the sales Joe has checked; until then draft is true and the page says so.

items.name: Silver cake basket
items.marks: A lion for sterling, the crowned leopard’s head for London, the maker’s mark, and a long s: the London letter for 1753–54.
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Agateware teapot
items.marks: No mark. Staffordshire potters rarely marked these; the marbled clay, the molding and the lion on the lid date it.
items.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Arita dish
items.marks: The base reads Da Ming Jiajing nian zhi, the mark of a Chinese emperor who reigned 1522–66. The dish is Japanese and later: the mark was borrowed, as was common.
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Rookwood vase
items.marks: The RP monogram with four flames: 1890. The incised initials are the decorator’s.
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Tiffany Favrile vase
items.marks: Engraved L.C.T. with a number under the foot. The pitted “Cypriote” surface imitates excavated ancient glass.
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Bronze of Henry Ward Beecher
items.marks: Signed J.Q.A. Ward, with the Gorham foundry mark on the base.
items.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access

items.name: Currier & Ives, Winter Morning in the Country
items.at: on the wall by the fireplace
items.marks: Hand-colored lithograph. The title and the publisher are printed under the image.

items.name: Singer treadle
items.marks: Serial G 7572 is in the block Singer gave the Model 27 on January 1, 1910. Singers were made by the million, and most sell for less than a new machine.

items.name: Leica III
items.marks: No. 140890 on the top plate dates the body to 1934.

items.name: Waltham pocket watch
items.at: in the jewelry box on the dresser
items.marks: Serial 13477185 on the movement: about 1903, 15 jewels. The case metal decides most of the price.

items.name: Letters home
items.marks: No sale can price these. Heirloom counts them as unknown, never as zero.
